findings.title: Cache status is not refreshed after deleting cached data
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation, it does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Unless the parent happens to pass an onSuccess that refetches, `cacheUpdatedAt` stays on screen after a successful delete, so the 'Cache Status' line keeps showing a timestamp for data that no longer exists.

findings.title: Timestamp is always formatted in en-US, ignoring the user's locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` hardcodes the locale even though the component uses `useLocale()` for every other string. Users on other locales see an English date format inside a localized sentence. The locale from `useLocale` should be passed instead.

findings.title: Comment on updatedAt is inaccurate and @updatedAt has broader effects than described
findings.body: The comment says the default is for 'legacy rows and future raw inserts', but the field's purpose is to track the last cache write. `@updatedAt` makes Prisma stamp the column on every client update, which is what the feature relies on, and the comment does not say so. Also, the migration's `DEFAULT NOW()` gives every pre-existing cache row the migration time as its 'last updated' value, so the UI will show a misleading timestamp for legacy entries. This is not documented.

findings.title: Every cache refresh issues an unconditional UPDATE on all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential
findings.body: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs with an empty data object on every `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache`. It rewrites `updatedAt` on all selected calendars for the credential, including ones unrelated to the cache, and the PR notes say nothing in the frontend reads that value. This adds write load on a hot path for no functional gain. It should be removed, or the cache status should be read from CalendarCache, which it already is.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is BSD/macOS-only and fails on Linux
findings.body: The in-place edit uses `sed -i ''`, which GNU sed treats as a filename argument, so the script errors out on Linux and in CI containers. The script also hard-codes `../.env` relative to the working directory and does not check that `tmole` is installed before using it. It is also unrelated to the cache feature this PR is about.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without tsx being declared as a dependency
findings.body: `npx tsx` downloads tsx on demand if it isn't installed, and the version is unpinned, so the script behaves differently across machines. This change is also unrelated to the calendar cache feature and is not mentioned in the PR's review checklist.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation or the cache-status enrichment
findings.body: The authorization check (credential must belong to the caller) and the deletion of CalendarCache rows are new security-relevant behavior, but no unit or integration test covers them. Nor is there a test for `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` or for the `cacheUpdatedAt` mapping in `connectedCalendarsHandler`. The PR's test plan is manual only.

findings.title: Remove-app behavior changed for the error-state alert without being called out
findings.body: Previously the error-state alert showed the disconnect button whenever there was no delegationCredentialId. Now `canDisconnect` also requires `!disableConnectionModification`, and the error path also gets the cache dropdown. This is a behavior change that is not described in the PR summary and is not covered by the test plan.
